## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by narrow brown to grayish-brown wings, fine wavy markings, and relatively long palps that give the front of the head a slightly “long-horned” appearance. In Florida, the Long-horned Owlet is likely found in warm wooded, shrubby, or semi-open habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and yards where adults may come to lights. Its caterpillar host plants appear poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small nocturnal plant-feeding moth whose larvae likely feed on low vegetation or leaf litter while supporting birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
